heading: India News Live Updates, 15 September 2026 |BRS files breach of privilege notice against Telangana CM Revanth Reddy
paragraphs: The Bharat Rashtra Samithi (BRS) on Thursday submitted a breach of privilege notice against Telangana Chief Minister A Revanth Reddy, accusing him of making false allegations against party president K Chandrasekhar Rao during his Assembly speech.
BRS MLAs G Mahipal Reddy and B Laxma Reddy handed over the notice to the Assembly Secretary, seeking action against Reddy for allegedly displaying fake documents and making misleading statements.

Delhi woke up to a warm and cloudy morning today, with light rain expected during the day. According to the weather department, the minimum temperature settled at 27.2 degrees Celsius, over two degrees above normal, while the maximum is expected to be around 33 degrees Celsius.

The BJP secured a clear majority in the 100-member Kota Municipal Corporation, winning 55 wards against Congress’s 40, while three seats went to Independents. But results in three Kota wards and one ward in Suket were put on hold after EVM glitches, with re-polling scheduled for September 16 and counting on September 17. After the dispute over Ward 87, Congress candidate Laxmi Sharma stage a dharna outside the counting centre, alleging foul play and demanding transparency.

Three Italian nationals travelled from Delhi to Munich without going through immigration at the Delhi airport on September 4. The incident prompted the Ministry of Civil Aviation (MoCA) to issue a show-cause notice to Air India, sources said.

The three passengers had taken an Air India “hub-and-spoke” flight on the night of September 3 from Amritsar to Delhi, after which they boarded a Lufthansa flight to Munich early on September 4 without going through immigration.

Given the serious nature of the lapse, Union Home Secretary Govind Mohan is likely to soon hold a meeting with stakeholders, including top officials at MoCA, Bureau of Immigration, Air India and airport operator Delhi International Airport.

The Bharat Rashtra Samithi (BRS) on Thursday submitted a breach of privilege notice against Telangana Chief Minister A Revanth Reddy, accusing him of making false allegations against party president K Chandrasekhar Rao during his Assembly speech.
BRS MLAs G Mahipal Reddy and B Laxma Reddy handed over the notice to the Assembly Secretary, seeking action against Reddy for allegedly displaying fake documents and making misleading statements.
Separately, BRS leaders approached the cybercrime police over an allegedly fake social media account and complained about alleged police high-handedness against their women MLAs.
Three labourers were killed and 11 injured when the roof slab of an under-construction Church of South India building collapsed while workers were pouring concrete in Vellore district on Thursday.

The incident occurred at Mandi Krishnapuram near Katpadi, where the 20-foot steel scaffolding and support structure suddenly gave way, trapping workers under concrete debris. The injured were taken to hospitals in Vellore and neighbouring Chittoor.

NDRF, police, fire services and district officials joined the rescue operation. The district administration will form a committee to investigate the structural failure and verify whether all required approvals and building permits had been obtained.

Delhi Lieutenant Governor Taranjit Singh Sandhu has approved the creation of 427 ancillary posts for 53 newly created courts of the Delhi Higher Judicial Service (DHJS) established for Fast Track Special Courts.
The posts include readers, judicial assistants, stenographers, Ahlmads, assistant Ahlmads, drivers and multi-tasking staff. The proposal has a financial implication of Rs 37.37 crore.
The Finance Department, however, said 243 vacant ancillary posts in the existing 415 courts should be filled on priority before the new posts are operationalised.

Two people were killed and 12 others injured after a truck rammed into a tempo on the Pune-Bengaluru highway near Jambhulwadi around midnight. After the collision, the truck and tempo crossed onto the opposite carriageway and hit two cars. Three of the injured are in serious condition. Police have registered a case against the truck driver and owner.

A three-day roundtable conference to draw up an implementation roadmap for 73 major projects announced in Kerala’s 2026-27 Budget will begin in Thiruvananthapuram on Wednesday. The ‘Reimagining Kerala’ conferences, to be held from September 16 to 18, will bring together ministers, senior bureaucrats, experts, investors and other stakeholders.

The initiative, organised under the theme “Ideas, Projects, Actions”, will involve more than 40 government departments and agencies. Discussions will focus on the vision, ownership, resources and implementation strategy for the projects, including funds required, lead departments and preparation of Detailed Project Reports. The first day will focus on industrial and technology initiatives, while subsequent sessions will cover social development, tourism, startups, transport and disaster management.

Independents have swept nearly two-thirds of the urban wards across Rajasthan Chief Minister Bhajanlal Sharma's home turf of Bharatpur and neighbouring Deeg, a concentration significantly higher than in the adjoining eastern districts of the state.

The results assume political significance as the region is the chief minister's bastion, where the BJP holds five of its seven Assembly seats, while Nagar MLA Jawahar Singh Bedham is the minister of state for home in Sharma's Cabinet.
Sharma hails from Bharatpur but represents the Sanganer Assembly constituency in Jaipur.

Independents have won 262 of the 415 wards across 13 urban local bodies in Bharatpur and Deeg districts, which together made up the erstwhile Bharatpur district, accounting for 63.1 per cent of all wards in the two districts.
The BJP won 131 wards, or 31.6 per cent, while the Congress managed just 19, or 4.6 per cent. The BSP won two wards and the RLP one.
Independents emerged as the largest category in each of the 13 urban local bodies across Bharatpur and Deeg, showing that the trend was not confined to Bharatpur city, the chief minister's hometown.
The results also present a contrast with the region's representation in the state Assembly. PTI
Bihar Deputy Chief Minister Vijay Kumar Chaudhary on Tuesday said the JD(U) will study the Uniform Civil Code Bill and will "not oppose it for no reason" if provisions are unexceptionable.

The former state JD(U) president made the statement at the party office where he was addressing a press conference, and replying to queries about the political turbulence that has ensued after Union Home Minister Amit Shah's assertion that UCC will be implemented "across 22 NDA-ruled states by 2029".

Chaudhary, who is also a former state assembly speaker, sought to distance the JD(U) from the strident stance adopted by RJD, the main party in opposition, which has vowed to thwart the UCC's implementation in Bihar, alleging that it was "against the interests of Muslims". PTI
Chief Minister of Keralam V D Satheesan on Tuesday said that democratic values across the world were facing new challenges and urged everyone to uphold truth and protect liberty.

He made the remarks in a post on 'X' while extending his greetings on the occasion of International Day of Democracy and called for reaffirming the commitment to the values that lie at the heart of the Indian Republic.
Democracy was not just an exercise of an electoral mandate, but "an enduring commitment to pluralism, equality, dignity and justice".
It is sustained by strong institutions, an informed citizenry and the freedom to question, participate and be heard, he added.

"At a time when democratic values across the world face new challenges, we must renew our faith in the foundational idea of India- an India strengthened by its diversity, anchored in secularism and constitutionalism, and united through the spirit of federal cooperation." PTI

The Maharashtra government on Tuesday constituted a committee headed by Environment Minister Pankaja Munde to examine a proposal to increase the amount of deposits taken from industrial units as bank guarantees for abiding by environmental norms and not causing pollution.
The committee, set up through a Government Resolution (GR), will also suggest technical and policy measures to curb air and water pollution.
The move came months after the Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) flagged serious lapses in the collection and enforcement of such guarantees.
The committee will study, in consultation with experts, increasing the deposit amount, the GR said.

The CAG report tabled during the Budget session earlier this year had pointed out that 2,678 bank guarantees worth Rs 272.47 crore had not been obtained in physical form, making them unverifiable. Forfeiture orders could not be executed in several cases because the guarantees had not been collected.

The CAG had also said that Rs 17.98 crore from forfeited guarantees were incorrectly credited instead of being used for environmental remediation. It had also flagged short recovery of Rs 7.56 crore in consent fees and said environmental compensation of Rs 183.25 crore imposed on 339 industries remained unrecovered, with notices subsequently withdrawn without justification. PTI

Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary on Tuesday said Bihar received less than 30 per cent of rainfall so far this year, but is still suffering a devastating flood due to heavy downpour in bordering states and neighbouring Nepal.
Choudhary was speaking at a programme where he transferred Rs 579.23 crore in relief assistance to the bank accounts of 8.27 lakh flood-affected families in 15 districts, each receiving Rs 7,000.
Around 49.72 lakh people have been affected by floods in the state, with several rivers flowing above their danger marks, the Disaster Management Department said.
Choudhary directed the district magistrates of the affected districts to prepare detailed reports on flood-related damage ahead of Union Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan's visit on Wednesday.
A central team led by Chouhan will visit the state to assess the flood situation. PTI

Indian solo traveller Arunima I P, alias Backpacker Arunima, sparked concern after posting a distress message on social media on Monday, claiming that she had been detained by the Taliban during her ongoing trip to Afghanistan. Arunima, who had sought the help of the Indian Embassy, however, said on Tuesday that she was safe.

A native of Ottapalam in Kerala’s Palakkad, Arunima had shared a video on her YouTube channel on Monday saying that she was detained by Taliban as they do not allow women travelling alone in Afghanistan. She had also put out a message stating: “Please help me connect to the Indian embassy.’’ However, on Tuesday morning, she wrote: “I am safe.’’

Arunima, who reached Afghanistan last month and had since been travelling alone, said her trip in the country has been attracting crowds everywhere as women were not seen at public places there. Read Here

Around 200 SpiceJet passengers protested at Delhi airport after two flights to Dubai were repeatedly rescheduled and delayed since Monday, according to sources, PTI reported. Flights SG 5111 and SG 5105, scheduled to depart from Terminal 3 on Monday morning and evening were delayed due to operational issues following the grounding of an aircraft. The airline said it was arranging alternate flights for affected passengers and regretted the inconvenience caused. Airport officials have also taken up the matter with SpiceJet executives.

Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary transferred Rs 579.23 crore in relief assistance to 8.27 lakh flood-affected families across 15 districts. Each family received Rs 7,000, officials said. Nearly 49.72 lakh people have been affected by the floods following heavy rainfall over the past two to three days, with several rivers continuing to flow above normal levels, according to the Disaster Management Department. Choudhary directed district magistrates to prepare detailed reports on the flood damage ahead of Union Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan’s visit to the state on Wednesday. A central team led by Chouhan will assess the flood situation and the extent of damage.

Kerala Chief Minister V D Satheesan reviewed the draft Kerala Policy for Elders and the Kerala State Elderly Persons (Care and Protection) Bill 2026 at a high-level meeting as the government works towards stronger legal safeguards and welfare for senior citizens. A separate department is formed for senior citizens by the Congress-led UDF government, a promise made in its Assembly election manifesto. "We have to protect every elderly person. We will not allow them to be alone. The government is with them. Keralam is with them. That is the message," the chief minister said.

The Supreme Court asked the Centre to consider extending the tenure of retiring tribunal chairpersons and members for a month or so to ensure that the quasi-judicial bodies do not become defunct due to vacancies. A bench headed by Chief Justice Surya Kant said the Centre should ensure that appointments are made without delay, noting that fresh vacancies could lead to another round of litigation if tribunals are left without enough members. The Centre told the court that the appointment process has already begun under the Tribunal Reforms Act, 2026 and opposed requests for ad hoc extensions. However, the court said it did not want the functioning of tribunals to be disrupted and asked the government to consider continuing the existing arrangement temporarily.

The court also noted that three members of the National Green Tribunal, two judicial and one technical, were due to retire. As an interim measure, it extended their tenure until fresh appointments are made.

Gurgaon Police detained Kalyan Bainsla today, the driver accused of ramming his car into a woman riding a sports bike on Golf Course Road, and said he would be brought to Gurgaon for questioning before being formally arrested. Police have also added an attempt to murder charge under Section 109 of the BNS to the FIR. The car, a white Maruti Suzuki Ciaz, belongs to an Army personnel posted in Assam and had been borrowed by Bainsla two days before the incident, police said. The incident, captured on video and widely shared on social media, took place on Sunday when the woman, identified as Delhi-based biker Sia, was riding with a group. Police said CCTV footage showed the car allegedly swerving into her lane and hitting the bike. Sia has rejected Bainsla's claims that the bikers were speeding and cutting him off, and questioned why he did not stop after the collision if he was remorseful.

A woman in Delhi received a call from a person claiming to be Canada-based gangster Goldy Brar, who demanded Rs 200 crore as extortion money, police sources said, as per PTI. The demand is believed to be the highest extortion amount sought in the national capital so far. A case was registered at the Civil Lines police station following a preliminary inquiry, while the Delhi Police Special Cell is also probing the matter.

Four family members were killed and 2 others are seriously injured after a refrigerator exploded at their home in Chavat Galli in Belagavi, a city in Karnataka. The fire quickly spread through the house, trapping the family members inside, police said. All were rushed to a hospital and the injured are undergoing treatment.

Delhi woke up to a warm and cloudy morning today, with light rain expected during the day. According to the weather department, the minimum temperature settled at 27.2 degrees Celsius, over two degrees above normal, while the maximum is expected to be around 33 degrees Celsius.

Landslides struck the Karmatar and Upper Bullung areas of West Sikkim, blocking the road today. The residents were soon evcuated as a precaution. A landslide beneath a local school in Karmatar was reported Monday morning, after which an SSB disaster rescue team was deployed.

Another landslide at Upper Bullung blocked a road to vehicular traffic. No casualties, injuries or property damage were reported, officials said. Heavy earth-moving machinery has been requisitioned to clear the debris and restore traffic. (PTI)
